h: פָּרָשַׁת כִּי תֵצֵא, א׳ Ki Seitzei, 1
Torah and Shema Win the Inner War of Elul

p: "When you go out to war against your enemies" (Devarim 21:10).
In the Zohar Chadash on this parashah:
What is 'Yisrael has cast off the good'?
and this is the holy Torah, etc.;
for there is no accusing force
why does it need words of Torah?
The yetzer tov is crowned with them,
and the yetzer hara is subdued by them.
'When you go out to war against your enemies'
for we must go out against it
and to wage war against it;
it will be delivered into the hand of the person,
'And Hashem your God will deliver him into your hand.'"
that the victory comes through the Torah,
only "And Hashem your God will deliver him into your hand."
the yetzer tov against the yetzer hara,
that a person has the power by himself
לְהַרְגִּיז יֵצֶר טוֹב עַל יֵצֶר הָרָע
to incite the yetzer tov against the yetzer hara;
for so there were created in a person
"a wise man's heart at his right,
and a fool's heart at his left";
and the wise heart always inclines to good,
to love and fear of Hashem Yisbarach,
and the yetzer hara the opposite.
And he can by himself incite
and make the yetzer hara tremble,
שֶׁמֶּלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
that the King of kings, HaKadosh Baruch Hu,
stands over him and sees his deeds;
and immediately there will come to him
out of dread of Hashem Yisbarach
(as is written in the Hagahah at the beginning of Orach Chaim),
and through this he will refrain from sinning.
at the time of the yetzer hara
no one remembers the yetzer tov.
For this it gives the advice:
he should occupy himself with Torah,
drag it to the beis midrash";
for the Torah is the antidote to the yetzer hara,
I created Torah as its antidote."
which came to rectify the great anger,
"For in much wisdom is much anger."
And this is the meaning of
the beis midrash is called a place
And this is the antidote to the yetzer hara,
to rectify "the fool's heart at his left";
and as it says in the holy Zohar:
and were it not that HaKadosh Baruch Hu
for the yetzer hara can sometimes enter
even into one occupied with Torah.
and there is no power at all
then with this he will certainly
be able to defeat the yetzer hara.
in the Zohar Chadash cited above
which is written in the first paragraph
which is the unity and love of Hashem,
of itself inclines toward the good,
that is, to the unity and love of Hashem.
For all the mitzvos in the Torah
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב פב, ב)
the Torah gives a person, etc."
he will fix in his heart the utterance
which is the sum of the whole Torah.
And here, where it is written,
"And Hashem your God will deliver him into your hand"
that is, that there be fixed in his heart
that is, that he should know
that He is the Master of all the powers,
and He shows a person his way,
how to walk in His ways,
that is, through words of Torah,
shall come the case of both of them"
the way in which he should go.
And this is the meaning of "your God":
he will defeat the yetzer hara.
why does it need words of Torah?"
שֶׁאִם הָיָה מֵבִיא הַפָּסוּק (דְּבָרִים יא, יג)
For had he brought the pasuk (Devarim 11:13):
"And to serve Him with all your heart,"
which is in the second paragraph of the Shema
even though there too it says
which means with both your inclinations
"And it shall be, if you listen diligently
and for this one needs the words of Torah,
to know the way in which to go,
"Fortunate are those whose way is perfect,
who walk in the Torah of Hashem";
he would not know the good way,
But since he brings the pasuk
which is said in the first paragraph,
the unity and love of Hashem;
and it is written "upon your heart (levavecha),"
and he expounded it as your two inclinations
to love and the unity of Hashem Yisbarach;
so why does it need for this
that the yetzer tov is crowned with them:
for through the words of Torah
that enter and become fixed in the heart,
there is made a crown for his head,
these are the tefillin of the head";
that is, he is bound up with them
"and the yetzer hara is subdued by them."

p: And afterward it says in the Zohar Chadash:
"'And she shall weep for her father
and her mother a full month'
this is the month of Elul,
in which Moshe ascended the mountain
And in the sefer Avodas Yisrael
by the holy Maggid of Kozhnitz,
may the memory of the holy tzaddik be blessed,
as referring to the month of Elul,
and with his broad mind he arrived at
the words of the Zohar Chadash.
"And Hashem your God will deliver him into your hand,"
which is what is indicated by
"And she shall weep for her father and her mother"
עַל מַה שֶּׁלֹּא נִצַּח עַד עַתָּה
over his not having defeated until now
"And Hashem your God will deliver him."
"He who robs his father and his mother" (Mishlei 28:24)
as referring to HaKadosh Baruch Hu
we call it Torah she'b'al peh."
For he had a counsel beforehand,
as the Gemara cited above says:
these days in the month of Elul,
when Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, ascended
and to receive the second Luchos,
now that you have been distressed,
And through the Torah she'b'al peh
one can rectify the great anger,
"For in much wisdom is much anger"
is needed for the great anger,
"And she shall weep for her father
and her mother a full month"
'And after that you may come to her
is the day on which were given
when there were given to Moshe
and pronounces the holy Name as it is written,
"And Hashem your God will deliver him."
are called "those who fear My Name,"
the awe of Shabbos is upon him;
and then he can take to heart
שֶׁמֶּלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
that the King of kings, HaKadosh Baruch Hu,
stands over him and sees his deeds.
is to be made entirely Torah,
And Shabbos is a time of teshuvah,
"It is good to give thanks (lehodos) to Hashem,"
'And one who confesses and forsakes them shall find mercy.'"
And the Shabbosos of this month
are especially suited to rectify everything,
